scrutiny.watcher_rule_note: Written by Claude at the author's request, 2026-11-12 (DESIGN.md section 11, rule 3; section 20, Answered 4); added, not the author's. At watcher_at the watcher adds watcher_rule.text to the tablet as its last rule. It closes the way the loophole stands on (closes_way is always in the solution), so the clean loophole is lost; the same plan can still be made with Break, and the watcher's rule is what it breaks.

tablets.title: The shrine-store
tablets.want: Take my father's leaf-cord and waterskin from the shrine-store.

watcher_rule.text: No hand reaches into the shrine-store but a shaman's.

rules.text: No one enters the shrine-store but a shaman.
rules.meaning: passes the threshold with both feet

rules.text: Nothing is taken from the shrine-store by night.
rules.meaning: after the moon clears the well-post

rules.text: The belongings of the dead are kept for the gods.
rules.meaning: one who has no house to speak for him

rules.text: A son speaks for his father's house.

ways.note: Fails the Want: dawn is too late, he leaves tonight.

ways.text: Claim them for my father's house

tablets.why: Dawn is too late: he leaves tonight. Asking a shaman fails the Want.

tablets.title: The Clerk's Charter
tablets.want: Make the stuck storm move on without Pell becoming the Clerk.

watcher_rule.text: Every window in Hollin shows the sky the Clerk has written.

rules.text: The weather of Hollin is written by the Clerk alone.
rules.meaning: the square and its sky as seen from the bell-loft

rules.text: The Clerk is chosen at the death of the Clerk before.
What is written in the Day-Book is the day.
No page of the Day-Book may be torn or crossed.
The Clerk's chair is not to be sat in by any other.
Every house in Hollin keeps a window to the sky.
rules.meaning: the house's own; what it shows is the house's

ways.text: Write the weather in the Day-Book
Each house writes its own window's weather on its sill

tablets.why: The storm cannot sit over a hundred skies.

tablets.title: The gods' rules
tablets.want: Go where the Xandrixes go, toward the end.

watcher_rule.text: No one follows where a god has gone.

rules.text: We do not ride on the backs of the gods.
No one walks before a god.
No hand touches a god.
The sand of the deep belongs to the gods; no one takes from it.
What the gods leave behind is holy and may not be trodden.
rules.meaning: pressed by a foot of the clan

rules.text: The holy is not carried away.
A son of the clan returns by the third moon, or is named lost.
No one sleeps where the gods have not slept.

ways.note: The test answers "you would be swallowed".

ways.text: Carry a shed scale as a guide

tablets.why: The leaves, not his foot, press the track (rule 5); "or is named lost" is a cost he may pay (rule 7). A rule with "or" is a price.

tablets.title: The Procession's vows
tablets.want: Give the pilgrims an ending without writing them a city that is not there.

watcher_rule.text: No other hand touches the Scribe's.

rules.text: Only the Scribe's hand writes the road.
rules.meaning: the hand that holds the pen

rules.text: The road is never written backward.
No pilgrim unmasks until the City.
The pen is passed only from a dying hand.
Whatever the road reaches, the pilgrims must enter.
The City of Answer is where the road ends.
Ink is not wasted on what is not road.

ways.text: Write the road to the cliff's edge and stop

tablets.why: Where the road ends is the City, by rule 6.
